title: Separatedness descends along flat surjective quasi-compact morphisms (Stacks 02KU)
statement: Let $g:S'\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] which is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism] and quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes and let $f':X\times_SS'\to S'$ be the second projection of the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product]. If $f'$ is separated [def-weil-proper-morphism] (its diagonal $X\times_SS'\to(X\times_SS')\times_{S'}(X\times_SS')$ is a closed immersion), then $f$ is separated.

source.place: Descent, Lemma Tag 02KU (lemma-descending-property-separated, line 5581: 'The property P(f) = "f is separated" is fpqc local on the base'), the direction 'the base change has P => f has P' of Definition Tag 02KO (definition-property-morphisms-local, line 5310) for the one-member fpqc covering $\{g:S'\to S\}$. The one-member family $\{g\}$ is then an fpqc covering of $S$ (Topologies, Lemma Tag 03L7, lemma-recognize-fpqc-covering, topologies.tex line 2904, (2): for an affine open $U\subseteq S$ the open $g^{-1}(U)$ is quasi-compact and $g(g^{-1}(U))=U$)

proof.text: *Step 1 ($\Delta_{f'}$ is universally closed).* Write $X'=X\times_SS'$ for the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] of $f$ and $g$, with projections $g':X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to S'$, $f\circ g'=g\circ f'$. By hypothesis $f'$ is separated, i.e. its diagonal $\Delta_{f'}:X'\to X'\times_{S'}X'$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-proper-morphism]. A closed immersion is universally closed by clause (d) of [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-integral-separated-uc] (Stacks Morphisms, Lemma 01W5); so $\Delta_{f'}$ is universally closed. (Source: '$\Delta'$ ... is a closed immersion, hence universally closed.')

source.place: Descent, Lemma Tag 02KU (lemma-descending-property-separated), proof, lines 5585-5602: 'let $S'\to S$ be a flat surjective morphism ... Assume that the base change $f':X'\to S'$ is separated. This means that $\Delta':X'\to X'\times_{S'}X'$ is a closed immersion, hence universally closed. Note that $\Delta'$ is the base change of $\Delta:X\to X\times_SX$ via $S'\to S$. By Lemma [02KS] this implies $\Delta$ is universally closed. Since it is an immersion (Schemes, Lemma [01KJ]) we conclude $\Delta$ is a closed immersion.'

proof.text: *Step 2 ($\Delta_{f'}$ is, up to an isomorphism of its target, the base change of $\Delta_f$ along a base change $h$ of $g$).* Let $P=X\times_SX$ with structure morphism $\pi=f\circ\mathrm{pr}_1:P\to S$, and $\Delta_f:X\to P$ the diagonal, so $\pi\circ\Delta_f=f$. Let $P'=P\times_SS'$ be the fibre product of $\pi$ and $g$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with projections $h:P'\to P$ and $\pi':P'\to S'$, and let $\delta=\Delta_f\times_S\mathrm{id}_{S'}:X'=X\times_SS'\to P'$ be the induced morphism, so $h\circ\delta=\Delta_f\circ g'$ and $\pi'\circ\delta=f'$. (a) By [lemma-nagata-diagonal-base-change] (with $X_\lambda\to S_\lambda$ the morphism $f:X\to S$ and $S\to S_\lambda$ the morphism $g:S'\to S$; its Lean is CategoryTheory.Limits.diagonal_pullback_fst), the base change $\delta$ of $\Delta_f$ is canonically identified with $\Delta_{f'}$: there is an isomorphism $c:X'\times_{S'}X'\to P'$ (the canonical identification $(X\times_SS')\times_{S'}(X\times_SS')\cong(X\times_SX)\times_SS'$) with $c\circ\Delta_{f'}=\delta$. (b) The square with top $g':X'\to X$, left $\delta$, right $\Delta_f$ and bottom $h:P'\to P$ is cartesian: in the diagram whose lower square is the cartesian square $(P',h,\pi')$ of $\pi$ and $g$, the outer rectangle consists of $g':X'\to X$, $\pi'\circ\delta=f':X'\to S'$, $\pi\circ\Delta_f=f:X\to S$ and $g$, and is cartesian because $(X',g',f')$ is a fibre product of $f$ and $g$; hence the upper square is cartesian by [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting], i.e. $(X',g',\delta)$ is a fibre product of $\Delta_f$ and $h$. (c) $\delta=c\circ\Delta_{f'}$ is universally closed: $\Delta_{f'}$ is by step 1, the isomorphism $c$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] (a homeomorphism onto the closed set $P'$ with $\mathcal O_{P'}\to c_*\mathcal O$ an isomorphism), hence universally closed by clause (d) of [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-integral-separated-uc], and a composition of universally closed morphisms is universally closed by clause (f) of the same node. (Source: 'Note that $\Delta'$ is the base change of $\Delta$ via $S'\to S$.')

source.place: Descent, Lemma Tag 02KU (lemma-descending-property-separated), proof, lines 5585-5602: 'let $S'\to S$ be a flat surjective morphism ... Assume that the base change $f':X'\to S'$ is separated. This means that $\Delta':X'\to X'\times_{S'}X'$ is a closed immersion, hence universally closed. Note that $\Delta'$ is the base change of $\Delta:X\to X\times_SX$ via $S'\to S$. By Lemma [02KS] this implies $\Delta$ is universally closed. Since it is an immersion (Schemes, Lemma [01KJ]) we conclude $\Delta$ is a closed immersion.'

proof.text: *Step 3 ($\{h:P'\to P\}$ is an fpqc covering of $P$).* The morphism $h$ is the base change of $g$ along $\pi$ (the first projection of the fibre product of $\pi$ and $g$). Hence $h$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] ($g$ flat), surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change] ($g$ surjective) and quasi-compact by clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] ($g$ quasi-compact). Let $V\subseteq P$ be an affine open. Since $h$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], $h^{-1}(V)$ is quasi-compact; it is covered by affine opens of $P'$ [def-pc-scheme], so by finitely many of them, $V_1,\dots,V_n$ ($n\ge0$), with $h^{-1}(V)=\bigcup_jV_j$. Since $h$ is surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism], $\bigcup_jh(V_j)=h(h^{-1}(V))=V$. Together with the flatness of $h$ this is the definition of an fpqc covering [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering] for the one-member family $\{h\}$. (This is Topologies, Lemma Tag 03L7 (2), lemma-recognize-fpqc-covering, written out; in the source the base $S'\to S$ is a morphism of affine schemes after the reduction of Lemma 02KP, and quasi-compactness is what that reduction secures; here $g$ is quasi-compact by hypothesis, so no reduction is needed.)

source.place: Topologies, Lemma Tag 03L7 (lemma-recognize-fpqc-covering, topologies.tex line 2904), clause (2); used implicitly in the proof of Descent 02KU at 'By Lemma [02KS] this implies $\Delta$ is universally closed', which applies 02KS to the covering $\{X'\times_{S'}X'\to X\times_SX\}$

proof.text: *Step 4 ($\Delta_f$ is universally closed, by descent of universal closedness, Descent 02KS).* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-universally-closed] to the morphism $\Delta_f:X\to P$ and the fpqc covering $\{h:P'\to P\}$ of step 3. Its hypothesis is that the second projection $X\times_PP'\to P'$ of the (chosen) fibre product of $\Delta_f$ and $h$ is universally closed. By step 2(b), $(X',g',\delta)$ is a fibre product of $\Delta_f$ and $h$, so by the uniqueness of fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product] there is an isomorphism $u:X\times_PP'\to X'$ with $\delta\circ u$ equal to that second projection; $u$ is universally closed (an isomorphism is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], clause (d) of [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-integral-separated-uc]) and $\delta$ is universally closed by step 2(c), so the second projection is universally closed by clause (f) of the same node. Hence $\Delta_f$ is universally closed. (Source: 'By Lemma [02KS] this implies $\Delta$ is universally closed.')

source.place: Descent, Lemma Tag 02KU (lemma-descending-property-separated), proof, lines 5585-5602: 'let $S'\to S$ be a flat surjective morphism ... Assume that the base change $f':X'\to S'$ is separated. This means that $\Delta':X'\to X'\times_{S'}X'$ is a closed immersion, hence universally closed. Note that $\Delta'$ is the base change of $\Delta:X\to X\times_SX$ via $S'\to S$. By Lemma [02KS] this implies $\Delta$ is universally closed. Since it is an immersion (Schemes, Lemma [01KJ]) we conclude $\Delta$ is a closed immersion.'

proof.text: *Step 5 ($\Delta_f$ is a closed immersion; $f$ is separated).* By step 4 and the definition of universally closed [def-weil-proper-morphism] applied to the base change along $\mathrm{id}_P$ (the fibre product of $\Delta_f$ and $\mathrm{id}_P$ is $X$ itself with second projection $\Delta_f$), $\Delta_f$ is a closed map of underlying spaces, so its image $\Delta_f(X)$ is closed in $P$. The diagonal $\Delta_f$ is an immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-diagonal-immersion] (Stacks Schemes, Lemma 01KJ). An immersion with closed image is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-closed-image-closed-immersion] (Stacks Schemes, Lemma 01IQ). Hence $\Delta_f:X\to X\times_SX$ is a closed immersion, i.e. $f$ is separated [def-weil-proper-morphism]. (Source: 'Since it is an immersion (Schemes, Lemma [01KJ]) we conclude $\Delta$ is a closed immersion. Hence $f$ is separated.' The step from 'universally closed immersion' to 'closed immersion' is Schemes 01IQ, which the source leaves implicit.)
